cues: Concentrated hydrochloric acid gives off fumes, so its strength drifts.
Potassium permanganate always contains a little manganese dioxide and is slowly reduced by traces of organic matter, so we standardise it freshly against oxalic acid.
text: The others fail too. Concentrated hydrochloric acid gives off fumes, so its strength drifts. Potassium permanganate always contains a little manganese dioxide and is slowly reduced by traces of organic matter, so we standardise it freshly against oxalic acid.
